newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Car explodes in Bahrain, no casualties.
newsitem.headline: Car explodes in Bahrain, no casualties.

text.p: A car exploded in the Bahraini capital on Saturday but a government official said it did not cause any damage or casualties.
"Investigations showed the explosion was caused by a a gas cylinder. There were no casualties or damage," the official told Reuters.
The blast occurred ahead of a trial of six Bahraini Shi'ite Moslems on Saturday on charges of possessing unlawful leaflets.
The six, arrested in April 1996, are Hassan Qassab, Shaker al-Mahouzi, Mirza al-Qatari, Saleh Hassan, Ali Isa Ahmed and Hussain Howaida, lawyers said.
"They were accused of possessing leaflets containing false news and statements without any reason," one lawyer said.
Shi'ite Moslems have launched sporadic attacks since December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms by the Sunni-led government.
Four people died on Friday in an arson attack on a shop in Manama. Officials said the blaze was premeditated.
Friday's attack was the latest in a series of fires to hit the island, the Gulf's main financial and banking centre, this week.
Seven Bangladeshi workers died in March 1996 when suspected arsonists set a restaurant ablaze on the small island of Sitra, linked with Manama by a three km (1.8 mile) causeway.
